- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥1.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +1.52 sentiment) by overshooting in next period — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak.
- If true price drops sharply after a spike, model often fails to correct — add a lagged correction: if last 3 days show downward trend, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5%.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon — if forecast is >1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.3–0.7σ.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to “stick” to recent trend — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values if sentiment is volatile.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently 0.5–1.0% below model, reduce forecast by 0.3–0.6% for next period — especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
